title: The Rise of CaaS: Context-as-a-Service for Agentic AI — Omer Primor, Bright Data
talk_summary: This talk is mostly a vendor pitch for web context services, but its transferable mechanism is measuring repeated context retrieval and owning/caching high-frequency context instead of renting it per query. It argues deterministic structured sources and freshness-aware refresh beat repeated LLM/search token burn for persistent knowledge work.

takeaways.technique: Own recurring context instead of renting per query
takeaways.what_they_do: They compare per-query AI search/CaaS against building a local structured dataset for repeated entity enrichment; owned retrieval has no added per-query AI cost.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every repeated query costs the same as the first even if it brought back the exact same answers
takeaways.numbers: Hypothetical setup: ~1 week and $5,000; tipping point just over 15,000 entities/queries in their test.

takeaways.technique: Instrument frequency to find build-vs-rent tipping point
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue frequency, not one-off query count, drives cost; measure repeated queries and compare rental cost to setup/maintenance of owned context.
takeaways.numbers: Tipping point just over 15,000 entities/queries; setup priced at ~1 week/$5,000.

takeaways.technique: Deterministic fetch from known structured sources
takeaways.what_they_do: For known sources they build scrapers/API pulls, merge entities with heuristics, and avoid LLM token cost for extraction/structuring.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Zero AI cost involved. There's no tokens.
takeaways.numbers: Coverage was 'fairly well. Not amazing' but with zero AI token cost; setup ~1 week/$5,000 hypothetical.

takeaways.what_they_do: They suggest using AI search/CaaS for ad hoc or unknown context and owned/deterministic indexes for persistent or known context, mixing per task.
takeaways.evidence_quote: maybe I need a combination of both maybe I can start seeing all sorts of cost efficiencies

takeaways.what_they_do: They note web data decays quickly, so context extraction is ongoing; owned context must be refreshed, not snapshotted once.
They note search results need token burn to structure, while CaaS pre-structures; they normalize entities into a schema once and reuse.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you also needed a lot of token burn it burn to actually structure that data
